lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: That name right there — flagged. Government sanctions list. You can't do business with it.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: And one hop back, that same party's hiding behind a name that looks completely clean on one of thousands of shipping manifests that cross every day.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So how did anyone even find it?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: That's what this is.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So you start with the raw manifest.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Every shipment starts as a messy file. This breaks it into its actual parts — shipper, value, vessel.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: But the name on here is clean.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: The name on here is clean. That's the point — it's supposed to be. Same pipeline's built to handle claims, transactions, whatever you throw at it. Right now it's a shipment.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Okay. So what do you do with a clean name?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: You trace it. The name on the form is a starting point. We follow who's behind that name — owned by whom — and we keep going until we hit the real thing.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: That's not the name on the manifest.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: One hop back. And that's the one from the beginning. Already flagged.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So if nobody traces it back—

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: —a sanctioned party does business through a name that looks clean on paper. The sanction exists, and it does nothing.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Whoever's actually behind this shipment — it's not even the name on the paperwork.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Right. A name-only check stops at the first name, looks fine, moves on. It never gets to hop two.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So does it just block it now?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: It doesn't decide on its own. It takes the chain, the hit, scores the shipment, and builds it all into one case file.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Somebody still has to look at it.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Somebody still puts their name on the decision. They're just not spending half a day reconstructing what we just watched happen in seconds.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: How do I trust that score? Or that flag?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: That's what this tab's for. Every rule that made that call is versioned. Every model's registered with a status. And if two signals disagree — which happens — a person looks at it. It doesn't get averaged out and forgotten.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So it's not just that you caught something.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Somebody's putting their name on this call. If it's wrong, that can't be 'the system said so.' They need to point to exactly why, months later.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: And everything you just watched — the ingest, the chain, the score, this tab — it's all the same two interfaces underneath. REST API, MCP.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So next week it's a claim, a transaction—

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Config change. That's kind of the whole point.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: That's UnmaskIQ, running on RiskModelForgeIQ's Decision Intelligence Layer. Demo link's in the comments.
